eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Age requirement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants aged ≥18 at the time of signing the ICF.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Wilson Disease diagnosis
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Diagnosis of WD by Leipzig Criteria ≥ 4 documented by testing as outlined in the 2012 European Association for the Study of Liver WD Clinical Practice Guidelines (Ferenci, 2003; EASL, 2012) or by historical test results for WD including some or all of the following: Presence of Kayser Fleischer rings, Neurological symptoms, Serum ceruloplasmin below reference range, Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia, Elevated liver or urinary copper, Presence of mutations in the ATP7B gene, or Other, as considered appropriate, may be used instead to confirm the diagnosis of WD.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Benefit from decoppering therapy
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants who in the opinion of the referring Investigator may benefit from decoppering therapy.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Ability to comply with study procedures
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants must be able to comply with all study-related procedures.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Ability to reside in CRU
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants must be able to reside in the CRU for intensive metabolic monitoring of copper and molybdenum.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Willingness to discontinue chelator therapy
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants willing to discontinue chelator therapy for approximately 4 days prior to initiation of ALXN1840 to allow a baseline assessment of copper balance.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Adequate venous access
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants with adequate venous access to allow collection of required blood samples.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Ability to swallow tablets
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants must be able to swallow intact ALXN1840 tablets.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Willingness to avoid copper/zinc/molybdenum minerals
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants willing to avoid use of minerals containing copper, zinc, or molybdenum throughout the study duration.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Willingness to adhere to controlled diet
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants willing to adhere to copper/molybdenum-controlled diet during inpatient periods and willing to comply with a low copper dietary requirement during the Outpatient Period.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Contraceptive use requirement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Contraceptive use by men or women should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies. Male participants: Male participants, if heterosexually active and with a female spouse or partner of childbearing potential or a pregnant or breastfeeding spouse or partner, must agree to use barrier contraception (male condom) for the duration of the study and for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Male participants must not donate sperm for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Female spouses or partners of male participants who are of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception as defined in Section 10.4, starting at least 1 menstrual cycle before (the male participant's) first study intervention administration and continuing until at least 3 months after the end of their male partner's systemic exposure to the study intervention. Barrier contraception (male condom) is required even with documented medical assessment of surgical success of a vasectomy. For male participants who have had a vasectomy (with documented evidence of azoospermia if possible) and agree to use a male condom for the stated time period, no additional contraceptive method is required by their female partner. Female participants: Female participants or female partners of male participants of childbearing potential (including breastfeeding females), if heterosexually active, must be willing to follow protocol-specified contraception guidance starting at least 1 menstrual cycle before first study intervention administration and continuing for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Female participants must not donate ova for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Female participants who are documented as being of non-childbearing potential as defined in Section 10.4 are exempt from contraception requirements.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Informed consent capability
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants capable of giving signed informed consent, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Decompensated cirrhosis or high MELD score
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Decompensated cirrhosis or model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) score > 13.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: High modified Nazer score
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Modified Nazer score > 7 (Dhawan, 2005).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent gastrointestinal bleed
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Clinically significant gastrointestinal bleed within past 3 months.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Elevated ALT
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) > 2 × upper limit of normal (ULN).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Marked neurological disease
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Marked neurological disease requiring assistance with self-care or activities of daily life.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Low hemoglobin
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Hemoglobin less than lower limit of the reference range for age and sex.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Active viral infection or HIV seropositivity
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Active infection with hepatitis B virus (positive hepatitis B surface antigen) or C virus (participants with positive hepatitis C antibody result would require confirmation of active disease with a positive hepatitis C polymerase chain reaction test), or seropositivity for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Significant medical history or current disorder
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: History or presence of/significant history of or current cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrinological, hematological, or neurological disorders, or psychiatric disorder that in the opinion of the Investigator may constitute a risk when taking the study intervention; or may interfere with the interpretation of data.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior ALXN1840 or tetrathiomolybdate treatment
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Previous treatment with ALXN1840 or other form of tetrathiomolybdate within 1 year prior to dosing.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior zinc treatment
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Previous treatment with zinc within 21 days prior to Day 1.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent experimental or unapproved therapy
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: The use of an experimental or unapproved/unlicensed therapy at the same time or within 90 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, prior to the Screening Visit.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Renal failure
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants in renal failure, defined as in end-stage renal disease on dialysis (chronic kidney disease [CKD] stage 5) or creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min (Levey, 2006).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Pregnancy or breastfeeding
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Pregnant (or females who are planning to become pregnant) or breastfeeding females (women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test result at screening).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Known sensitivity to ALXN1840 or excipients
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Known sensitivity to ALXN1840, ALXN1840 excipients (anhydrous dicalcium phosphate, anhydrous sodium carbonate), or any of the ingredients contained in ALXN1840 or related compounds.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Likely non-compliance
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: In the opinion of the Investigator, the participant and/or their legal guardian is likely to be non-compliant or uncooperative during the study.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History of illicit drug or significant alcohol abuse
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: History of illicit drug abuse, history of significant alcohol abuse within 1 year prior to the Screening Visit, or clinical evidence of substance and/or alcohol abuse within the 2 years before screening. Alcohol abuse is defined as regular weekly intake of more than 14 units (for both males and females), using the following National Health Service (NHS) alcohol tracker http://www.nhs.uk/Tools/Pages/drinks-tracker.aspx.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Positive urine drug toxicology screen
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Positive urine drug toxicology screen at Screening or on Day -8 (cannabinoids will not be tested).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent alcohol consumption or positive alcohol breath test
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Alcohol consumption within 48 hours prior to study intervention administration or positive alcohol breath test at screening or on Day -8.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Unwillingness to complete every meal and tolerate controlled menu
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participants unwilling to consistently complete every meal and tolerate a controlled, limited menu for the duration of the study.

substance.name: bis-choline tetrathiomolybdate
substance.description: Active pharmaceutical ingredient of ALXN1840; formerly known as WTX101. Each 15 mg ALXN1840 tablet contains 7.8 mg of tetrathiomolybdic acid. Excipients include anhydrous dicalcium phosphate and anhydrous sodium carbonate.

arms.name: ALXN1840 Treatment
arms.description: All participants receive ALXN1840 with dose titration starting at 15 mg/day for approximately 28 days (Day 1 through Day 28), followed by titration up to 30 mg/day beginning on Day 29 through Day 39. A Safety Review Committee reviews safety data before titration to 30 mg/day.

objectives.name: Primary Copper Balance Objective
objectives.text: Assess net copper balance with daily repeat-dose ALXN1840 treatment (15 mg and 30 mg) in participants with Wilson disease (WD)

endpoints.name: Primary Copper Balance Endpoint
endpoints.text: Mean daily copper balance where copper balance is measured by the calculated difference between copper intake (in food and drink) and copper output (in feces and urine) during ALXN1840 accumulation and steady-state periods for each dose

objectives.name: Secondary Copper Balance Change Objective
objectives.text: Assess change in copper balance in response to ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day during ALXN1840 accumulation and at steady state periods versus the pretreatment baseline in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Secondary Copper Balance Change Endpoint
endpoints.text: Change in mean daily copper balance as measured by the calculated difference between copper intake (in food and drink) and copper output (in feces and urine) from pretreatment baseline (Days -4 through -1) and ALXN1840 accumulation and steady-state periods for each dose

endpoints.name: Safety Endpoint - Clinical Laboratory Assessments
endpoints.text: Clinical laboratory assessments (serum chemistry, hematology, coagulation, and urinalysis)

objectives.name: Secondary Copper Disposition Objective
objectives.text: Investigate the effect of ALXN1840 (15 mg/day and 30 mg/day) on the disposition of copper in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Secondary Copper Disposition Endpoint
endpoints.text: Copper quantified in food, drink, feces, and urine, including plasma total and labile bound copper (LBC) during ALXN1840 accumulation and steady-state periods for each dose

objectives.name: Secondary Molybdenum Disposition Objective
objectives.text: Investigate the effect of ALXN1840 on the disposition of molybdenum at steady state at 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Secondary Molybdenum Disposition Endpoint
endpoints.text: Molybdenum quantified in food, drink, feces, and urine, plasma total molybdenum at ALXN1840 steady state

endpoints.name: Safety Endpoint - ECG
endpoints.text: Heart rate, intervals (PR, QRS, QT and QTc), and clinically significant electrocardiogram (ECG) findings as determined by triplicate 12-lead ECG

objectives.name: Secondary Molybdenum Balance Objective
objectives.text: Assess steady-state total molybdenum balance as a measure of ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Secondary Molybdenum Balance Endpoint
endpoints.text: Mean daily molybdenum balance as demonstrated through measurement of molybdenum intake (in food, drink and ALXN1840), and molybdenum output (feces and urine) representing ALXN1840 steady state

endpoints.name: Safety Endpoint - Vital Signs
endpoints.text: Vital sign assessments (blood pressure and heart rate)

objectives.name: Secondary Molybdenum Accumulation Objective
objectives.text: Assess accumulation of molybdenum with ALXN1840 treatment at 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Secondary Molybdenum Accumulation Endpoint
endpoints.text: Accumulation of molybdenum as determined by molybdenum balance

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
objectives.text: Determine the steady-state plasma pharmacokinetic (PK) of total molybdenum and plasma ultrafiltrate (PUF) molybdenum (as surrogate measures of ALXN1840, 15 mg and 30 mg) in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PK parameters for plasma total and PUF-molybdenum

objectives.name: Safety and Tolerability Objective
objectives.text: Evaluate the safety and tolerability of repeated-dose administration of ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Safety Endpoint - TEAEs and SAEs
endpoints.text: Treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs)/serious adverse events (SAEs)

objectives.name: Exploratory Dose Response Objective
objectives.text: Determine dose response of ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day for copper balance in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Exploratory Dose Response Endpoint
endpoints.text: Assess dose response of ALXN1840 on copper balance focusing on copper balance

objectives.name: Exploratory Treatment Duration Objective
objectives.text: Determine the effect of treatment duration on copper balance in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Exploratory Treatment Duration Endpoint
endpoints.text: Determine the effect of time following initiation of ALXN1840 treatment on copper balance

objectives.name: Exploratory Ceruloplasmin and Copper Profiles Objective
objectives.text: Assess the effects of ALXN1840 on ceruloplasmin, ceruloplasmin-bound copper LBC profiles in plasma in participants with WD

endpoints.name: Exploratory Ceruloplasmin and Copper Profiles Endpoint
endpoints.text: Ceruloplasmin, ceruloplasmin-bound copper, and LBC: Change in ceruloplasmin at Days 1, 8, 25, 29, 36, and Day 39 compared with predose

estimands.name: Primary Copper Balance Estimand - ALXN1840 15 mg/day
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Wilson Disease enrolled in the study who received ALXN1840 15 mg/day during inpatient periods (All Enrolled Participants (Full Analysis Set)) Summary measure: Mean daily copper balance (mg/day) with descriptive statistics including mean, standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval for each collection period.

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose reduction or interruption due to safety concerns
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant requires dose reduction or interruption of ALXN1840 15 mg/day due to meeting dose modification criteria before completion of the collection period

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose escalation to 30 mg/day
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant is escalated from 15 mg/day to 30 mg/day before the 15 mg/day steady-state collection period is complete

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation (Primary Copper Balance Estimand - ALXN1840 15 mg/day)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant discontinues the study prior to completing all collection periods for the 15 mg/day dose

intercurrentEvents.name: Outpatient period extension
intercurrentEvents.text: Outpatient period between inpatient periods is extended up to an additional 14 days, potentially affecting timing of steady-state assessment

intercurrentEvents.name: Incomplete dietary collection
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant fails to complete full copper-controlled diet intake or output collection during an inpatient collection period

estimands.name: Secondary Copper Balance Change Estimand - 15 mg/day vs Baseline
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Wilson Disease who completed the pretreatment baseline collection period (Days -4 through -1) and at least one ALXN1840 15 mg/day collection period (All Enrolled Participants with Baseline and Post-baseline Assessments (Full Analysis Set)) Summary measure: Change from baseline in mean daily copper balance (mg/day) with descriptive statistics; within-participant difference between treatment period and baseline.

intercurrentEvents.name: Incomplete baseline collection period
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant does not complete the full 4-day pretreatment baseline collection period (Days -4 through -1)

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose reduction or interruption during 15 mg/day collection
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant requires dose reduction or interruption before completing the 15 mg/day collection period

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before post-baseline assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant discontinues the study before completing any post-baseline ALXN1840 collection period

estimands.name: Secondary Copper Disposition Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Wilson Disease receiving ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day during inpatient periods (All Enrolled Participants (Full Analysis Set)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for copper concentrations and amounts in each matrix by dose and collection period.

intercurrentEvents.name: Incomplete sample collection for copper disposition
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant fails to provide complete fecal, urine, or blood samples during a collection period

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification during collection period (Secondary Copper Disposition Estimand)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant undergoes dose reduction or interruption during a copper disposition collection period

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation (Secondary Copper Disposition Estimand)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant discontinues the study prior to completing all copper disposition assessments

estimands.name: Secondary Molybdenum Disposition Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Wilson Disease receiving ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day at predicted steady state during inpatient periods (All Enrolled Participants (Full Analysis Set)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for molybdenum concentrations and amounts in each matrix at steady state by dose.

intercurrentEvents.name: Steady state not achieved
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant does not achieve molybdenum steady state within the planned collection period due to pharmacokinetic variability

intercurrentEvents.name: Incomplete molybdenum sample collection
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant fails to provide complete fecal, urine, or blood samples during the steady-state molybdenum collection period

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification during steady-state collection
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant undergoes dose reduction or interruption during the steady-state molybdenum collection period

estimands.name: Secondary Molybdenum Balance Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Wilson Disease receiving ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day at steady state during inpatient periods (All Enrolled Participants (Full Analysis Set)) Summary measure: Mean daily molybdenum balance (mg/day) with descriptive statistics; assessment of whether molybdenum(out) equals molybdenum(in) at steady state by dose.

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification during molybdenum balance collection
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant undergoes dose reduction or interruption during the molybdenum balance collection period at steady state

intercurrentEvents.name: Participant does not escalate to 30 mg/day (Secondary Molybdenum Balance Estimand)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant remains on 15 mg/day for the duration of the study due to safety concerns, precluding molybdenum balance assessment at 30 mg/day

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before steady-state molybdenum balance assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant discontinues the study before completing the steady-state molybdenum balance collection period

estimands.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Wilson Disease receiving ALXN1840 15 mg/day and 30 mg/day with adequate PK sampling during inpatient periods (PK Analysis Population (all participants with at least one evaluable PK sample)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics for PK parameters including AUC, Cmax, Cmin, Tmax, and half-life for plasma total and PUF-molybdenum by dose.

intercurrentEvents.name: Incomplete PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant misses one or more scheduled PK blood draws during the steady-state PK assessment period

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification during PK collection
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant undergoes dose reduction or interruption during the PK assessment period, affecting steady-state characterization

intercurrentEvents.name: Participant does not escalate to 30 mg/day (Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant remains on 15 mg/day for the duration of the study due to safety concerns, precluding PK characterization at 30 mg/day

intercurrentEvents.text: Participant discontinues the study before completing all planned ECG assessments

soaFootnotes.label: f
soaFootnotes.text: Discharge from the unit may occur after completion of all procedures on Day 9 and on Day 40 and after the Investigator has reviewed all safety assessment (including safety laboratory tests) and confirmed that the participant is appropriate for discharge.

soaFootnotes.label: g
soaFootnotes.text: A single outpatient visit or phone call and safety laboratory assessment should occur between Day 14 and Day 18. A phone call may take place on a different day than the blood draw within the Day 14 through Day 18 period.

soaFootnotes.label: i
soaFootnotes.text: Parameters include age and sex. Race and ethnicity will be collected where permitted by local regulations.

soaFootnotes.label: j
soaFootnotes.text: Wilson disease history will include diagnosis date, method of diagnosis, history of cirrhosis, details of any previous liver biopsies performed, and treatment received.

soaFootnotes.label: k
soaFootnotes.text: A full physical examination will be performed at Screening, at check-in for the study, and at the End of the study/Early Termination Visit. A physical examination should also be performed on any participants with ongoing adverse events prior to discharge from the unit. Otherwise, a symptom-driven physical examination may be performed at other times, at the Principal Investigator's discretion.

soaFootnotes.label: m
soaFootnotes.text: While in the CRU, study intervention will be administered after an overnight fast (ie, at least 10 hours) at the same time every morning; drug is to be administered with 240 mL of water and meals should be delayed a minimum of 2 hours after dosing. As an outpatient, participants are expected to take ALXN1840 at approximately the same time daily (+/-1 hour). Participants should take the medication with a glass of water on an empty stomach; meals should be delayed a minimum of 2 hours after dosing.

soaFootnotes.label: n
soaFootnotes.text: During the outpatient period, participants will use SMS text messaging to confirm study intervention administration.

soaFootnotes.label: o
soaFootnotes.text: Blood sampling for PK/PD will occur before ALXN1840 administration and represents a predose trough. See Table 2 for PK/PD sampling on Days 1, 25, 29, and 39.

soaFootnotes.label: p
soaFootnotes.text: PK/PD collection will include timepoints described in the schedule of PK/PD assessment for Days 1, 25, 29, and 39 (Table 2).

soaFootnotes.label: q
soaFootnotes.text: Samples for serum chemistry will be obtained following a fast of at least 8 hours at the Screening Visit and at check-in. In case of rechecks, and postdose serum chemistry, participants may not have fasted for 6 or 8 hours before the serum chemistry sample is taken.

soaFootnotes.label: r
soaFootnotes.text: Laboratory assessment including chemistry, hematology, and coagulation parameters should be performed on Days -8, -1, 8, 23, and 28 only.

soaFootnotes.label: s
soaFootnotes.text: Menstruation check for women only; women of childbearing potential should only be enrolled after a negative serum pregnancy test result at Screening. Additional urine pregnancy testing will be standard for the protocol unless serum testing is required by site policies, local regulation, or Institutional Review Boards (IRBs)/Independent Ethics Committees (IECs) (Section 10.2). In addition to pregnancy tests detailed at the visits in the SoA, females of childbearing potential will be required to perform urine pregnancy tests at least every 4 weeks at their home or the study site throughout their time in the study.

soaFootnotes.label: t
soaFootnotes.text: A single 15 mL serum sample will be retained for evaluation in the event of an unexpected safety finding; retained samples may be destroyed after completion of the clinical study report.

soaFootnotes.label: u
soaFootnotes.text: Vital signs measurements and ECGs should be performed predose, unless otherwise specified. Vitals signs include body temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

soaFootnotes.label: v
soaFootnotes.text: Copper- and molybdenum-controlled diet will be initiated after registration/inclusion. Participants will remain on a copper/molybdenum controlled diet throughout both the inpatient Period 1 (Day -8 to Day 9) and inpatient Period 2 (Day 23 to Day 40); during this time participants will be strongly encouraged to complete all meals. While not in the CRU, participants will be encouraged to adhere to their usual copper-controlled diet.

soaFootnotes.label: w
soaFootnotes.text: For each input/output balance period, 24-hour urine samples are to be collected for measurement of copper and molybdenum.

soaFootnotes.label: x
soaFootnotes.text: For fecal samples, each individual sample will be independently collected with record of date, time, and weight of the sample.

plannedDuration.reasonDurationWillVary: Duration depends on individual subject progression and follow-up.

eligibilityCriteria.name: Ability to comply with study procedures
Willingness to adhere to controlled diet
Decompensated cirrhosis or high MELD score
Active viral infection or HIV seropositivity
Significant medical history or current disorder
Known sensitivity to ALXN1840 or excipients
History of illicit drug or significant alcohol abuse
Recent alcohol consumption or positive alcohol breath test
Unwillingness to complete every meal and tolerate controlled menu

notes.text: This amendment is considered to be substantial based on the criteria set forth in Article 10(a) of Directive 2001/20/EC of the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union, the US Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) regulation at 21 CFR part 312.30(b), and any applicable local regulations.

The main reason for preparation of this amendment was to clarify study procedures occurring across different sites in the US, so as to facilitate participant recruitment across different regions of the US, and to lessen inconvenience for participants without compromising the quality of the study.
Addition of text to the footnote to state that procedures specific to screening sites (only in the US) detailed in Section 8. Rationale: As per Section 8 (below).

Number of days changed from 30 days to 21 days in the sentence regarding inhibitory effect of zinc on intestinal copper absorption after discontinuation of zinc. Rationale: To align the number of days with the mention of zinc discontinuation elsewhere in the protocol.

Addition of text applicable only to the US that details the possibility for sites in the US to only perform screening procedures and not any of the remaining study procedures. Rationale: To facilitate participant recruitment across different regions of the US and to lessen inconvenience for participants without compromising the quality of the study.
Abbreviations: ALT = alanine aminotransferase; AST = aspartate aminotransferase; IB = Investigator's Brochure; PK = pharmacokinetics; WD = Wilson disease.

The COVID-19 pandemic is active at the time of this protocol amendment. Given this unique circumstance, specific consideration has been given to the potential risks and mitigation measures due to COVID-19 vaccine (see Section 10.5).
A cannula may be placed to minimize needle sticks; however, a catheter may not be left in place for longer than 72 hours and should be flushed a minimum of every 8 hours.

Participants may be discharged from the CRU on Day 9 and return on Day 22 or Day 23 (predose); all procedures will start on Day 23. To ensure flexibility, the Outpatient Period during Treatment Period 1 may be extended up to an additional 14 days with Investigator approval.
During the Outpatient Period, participants will use SMS text messaging to confirm study intervention administration.
At the CRU's discretion, participants may remain in the CRU during the outpatient period for safety or to maintain the integrity of the conduct of the study.

This study incorporates the use of an adaptive design. Adaptive features may be implemented at the discretion of the Investigator to support conduct of the study. Such adaptive features do not require amendment of the protocol.
Abbreviations: CRF = case report form; CRU = clinical research unit; EOS = End of Study; SoA = Schedule of Activities.
Rescreened participants are not required to reconsent as long as they have signed the latest version of the ICF.

If a clinically significant finding is identified (including, but not limited to changes from baseline in QT interval corrected using Fridericia's formula [QTcF]) after enrollment, the Investigator or qualified designee will determine if the participant can continue in the study and if any change in participant management is needed. This review of the ECG printed at the time of collection must be documented.

Triplicate 12-lead ECGs will be conducted as outlined in the SoA (see Section 1.3) to obtain heart rate, PR, QRS, QT, and QTc intervals. As with vital signs, if ECG interval measurements are abnormal, an additional triplicate will be performed and recorded in the CRF.

Blood pressure and heart rate measurements should be preceded by at least 5 minutes of rest for the participant in a quiet setting without distractions (eg, television, cell phones). Ideally, the same arm for each participant should be used for measurements.

If vital signs are abnormal as defined by inclusion/exclusion criteria, 2 additional vital signs measurements will be made. The average of the 3 vital signs measurements will be recorded in the CRF and used to determine participant eligibility.

All laboratory tests with values considered abnormal and clinically significant during participation in the study or after the last dose of study intervention should be repeated until the values return to normal or baseline or are no longer considered clinically significant by the Investigator or Medical Monitor.

All SAEs will be recorded and reported to Alexion or the designee immediately and under no circumstance should this exceed 24 hours, as indicated in Section 10.3. The Investigator will submit any updated SAE data to Alexion within 24 hours of it being available.

Investigators are not obligated to actively seek AE or SAE data after conclusion of the study participation. However, if the Investigator learns of any SAE, including a death, at any time after a participant has been discharged from the study, and he/she considers the event to be reasonably related to the study intervention or study participation, the Investigator must promptly notify Alexion.
Open-ended and non-leading verbal questioning of the participant is the preferred method to inquire about AE occurrences.

A single biobanked serum sample will be collected predose from each participant to serve as a retained sample during the study. Samples will remain on site and will be discarded following the completion of the clinical study report. The sample will not be used for genetic testing.

For this study, any dose of ALXN1840 greater than that specified in the protocol will be considered an overdose. Alexion does not recommend specific treatment for an overdose. Overdoses are medication errors that are not considered AEs unless there is an untoward medical occurrence resulting from the overdose.
Samples collected within ± 10% or 30 min, whichever is less, of the scheduled time will not be considered a protocol deviation.

Excess/additional samples may be stored for up to 5 years and used for PD and/or diagnostic biomarker development and research to understand the pathways associated with the mechanism of action of ALXN1840. These samples will not be used for genetic analyses (ie, RNA or DNA analyses).
As this study is an exploratory study, no formal hypothesis testing is being conducted. Study results will be summarized using descriptive statistics.
Medical Monitor Name and Contact Information can be found in the Study Contact List.

I have read the study protocol amendment 3.1 and agree to conduct the study in accordance with this protocol, all applicable government regulations, the principles of the ICH E6 Guidelines for Good Clinical Practice, and the principles of the World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki. I also agree to maintain the confidentiality of all information received or developed in connection with this protocol.

Darwich, 2014 cited as reference for physiologic turnover of human gastrointestinal epithelial cells being 3-5 days, supporting the change from 30 to 21 days for inhibitory effect of zinc on intestinal copper absorption after discontinuation.

studyInterventions.name: ALXN1840
studyInterventions.description: bis-choline tetrathiomolybdate (formerly WTX101), a novel copper binding agent for the treatment of Wilson disease, administered as oral tablets at 15 mg/day for approximately 28 days followed by titration to 30 mg/day

studyInterventions.name: Paracetamol/acetaminophen
studyInterventions.description: Permitted for use as an exception with Investigator approval; maximum dose 1000 mg per day

studyInterventions.name: Ibuprofen
studyInterventions.description: Permitted with caution as a CYP2C9 substrate; must not exceed 1200 mg in any 24-hour period; may only be used with Investigator approval

studyInterventions.name: Penicillamine
studyInterventions.description: Copper-chelating therapy (standard of care for Wilson disease) that must be discontinued starting on Day -4 prior to ALXN1840 initiation to allow baseline copper/molybdenum balance assessment

studyInterventions.name: Trientine
studyInterventions.description: Copper-chelating therapy (standard of care for Wilson disease) that must be discontinued starting on Day -4 prior to ALXN1840 initiation to allow baseline copper/molybdenum balance assessment

studyInterventions.name: Zinc therapy
studyInterventions.description: Prior Wilson disease therapy that must be discontinued at least 21 days prior to Day 1 (zinc discontinuation required at Day -21 per Schedule of Activities)

studyInterventions.name: St John's wort / herbal remedies
studyInterventions.description: Disallowed; herbal remedies must be discontinued at least 7 days prior to first admission; St John's wort must be discontinued at least 2 weeks before first study intervention administration

studyInterventions.name: Prescription medications
studyInterventions.description: Disallowed within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) of Day -7 unless specifically permitted; nonprescription drugs (including vitamins and dietary or herbal supplements) disallowed within 7 days or 5 half-lives before Day -7 until follow-up visit completion

studyInterventions.name: Minerals containing copper, zinc, or molybdenum
studyInterventions.description: Disallowed throughout the study duration per inclusion criteria

studyInterventions.name: CYP2C9 and CYP2B6 substrate drugs
studyInterventions.description: Use with caution during co-administration with ALXN1840 per Investigator's Brochure guidance

studyInterventions.name: ALXN1840 or other tetrathiomolybdate
studyInterventions.description: Disallowed; previous treatment within 1 year prior to dosing is an exclusion criterion

studyInterventions.name: Experimental or unapproved/unlicensed therapy
studyInterventions.description: Disallowed within 90 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to Screening Visit
